messages:
jordan (Procure): FYI Vendor 'TokenFlow' sent renewal. Their pricing split is weird — commit vs metered, plus a separate "session" token line. Need quick eyes.

mika (Finance): Drop the headline numbers so I can run sensitivity.

jordan (Procure): Current baseline ~1.1B tokens/mo. Vendor offers commit $30k/mo covering 1.5B unique tokens; metered $0.018/1k; overage $0.014/1k. They say "unique" = post-dedupe.

owen (Platform): We already dedupe client-side; ask if their dedupe is global or per-tenant and what's the time window. Also: can we ingest their dedupe report?

jordan (Procure): Asked sales: "Confirm committed credits apply after your dedupe. Provide sample dedupe report + define session tokens. Any minimum seat fees?"

billing-bot: BillingOps: last TokenFlow invoice had a 7% variance vs our usage; ticket #1633 open.

tara (Legal): Add contract asks: quarterly reconciliations, right to audit redacted dedupe logs, and clear shortfall/true-up language. No automatic clawback beyond agreed true-up.

mika (Finance): If their dedupe is post-client and we get >20% net reduction, commit looks attractive. If not, metered + caps. I'll model three buckets and post results.

owen (Platform): I'll run a sampled dedupe on last 30 days and share net numbers by EOD. If vendor can provide S3 redacted reports in the same schema we can automate reconciliation.

jordan (Procure): Vendor replied: "Committed credits apply to post-dedupe unique tokens; session tokens count toward the commit; monthly redacted reports available; quarterly true-ups; no seat fees." They offered a 45-day POC with credits to validate.

tara (Legal): Approve POC but require audit clause + materiality threshold for billing errors.

jordan (Procure): TL;DR: POC + auditable reports + true-up likely tilt toward commit. If any piece missing, default to metered with negotiated hard cap.
